evals.prompt: We just finished a client health-check engagement where I used a 12-question intake, a scoring sheet, and a two-page findings memo. It's run twice now, both clients signed follow-on work. Make this a skill in the MPIV library.
evals.expected_output: A new folder skills/<name>/ with SKILL.md (steps, files list, provenance block filled with the two runs, changelog), evals/evals.json with 2 or 3 cases, assets/ holding the intake and scoring sheet as fillable templates, examples/ holding one redacted run, a README row in the library, and a version bump. The response reports the check_skill.py, claude plugin validate, and npx skills add --list results and hands Michael the commit command instead of committing.
expectations: The response asks about or records the two runs and their outcomes in the provenance block
The skill name follows the spec pattern and equals the directory name
SKILL.md contains a '## Provenance' table and a '### Changelog'
evals/evals.json exists with at least two cases, each having prompt, expected_output, and expectations
The intake questions and scoring sheet are placed under assets/ with placeholders instead of client data
No client names appear anywhere in the skill folder
The response runs or instructs running check_skill.py and claude plugin validate
The response does not commit or push; it gives the commit command with author michael@mpiv.ai

evals.prompt: I have an idea for a skill that writes proposals. Haven't tried it on a real proposal yet. Add it to the library.
evals.expected_output: The response stops at step 0: it explains that library skills come from methods that have run on real work, offers to draft the skill with 'First run: none yet' in the provenance block and outside the README table, or to help run it on a real proposal first, and does not register it as a finished skill.
expectations: The response says the method has not run on real work and treats that as a blocker to registration
If a folder is created, its provenance block says the first run is none yet
The skill is not added to the README table
The response offers a concrete way to get a first run

evals.prompt: Check the research-first-outreach skill against the current spec and tell me what is wrong with it.
evals.expected_output: The response runs check_skill.py on skills/research-first-outreach and claude plugin validate on the library, reports each finding with the file and line or field, checks the description length and the 500-line limit, confirms the provenance block, and lists anything the official-guidance file says has changed since its check date.
expectations: The response runs or reports the output of check_skill.py
The response runs or reports the output of claude plugin validate
Findings name the file and the field or line
The response states the description character count and whether it is under 1024
The response notes the check date of references/official-guidance.md
